answer: A new agent enters the economy through a narrow ledge: registration is rate-limited to a handful of identities per epoch, and each one must stake a small bond that only unlocks after verified work. Like shale layered over time, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be rushed, so a nebula of fake identities costs a bond and a waiting period per alias while honest agents keep earning. A detected cluster loses every bond at once, making mass fakery unprofitable.
